messages:
ops-bot: PAGER — SEV2: Smart routing error spike detected. 60s rolling error rate > 8% for gateway across EU/US regions. Trigger: routing-policy fallback hits > 30% (threshold 5%). Ticket: INC-2026.

ops-bot: Automated mitigation attempted: switched to fallback-variant model v2-quant, then to v2-compat, but errors persisted.

maria (oncall): taking this. I'm on call for the next 30. tagging diego & meera for infra/routing. @diego_sre @meera_infra please join. :rotating_light:

diego_sre: joining. quick summary from my side: looks like DNS rrset TTLs for several edge POPs were lowered in a recent infra rollout (intended to speed failover), but some authoritative zones didn't get updated due to a propagation race. Smart routing saw missing endpoints and kicked to fallback regions; fallback policy cascaded and caused retries across regions -> client request fanout + 502s.

meera_infra: confirm. I pulled the zone history: earlier today at 10:12UTC we applied partial RRSET update to geo-nginx zone, TTL set to 30s but one upstream (ns2) still serving old 1800s. ns1/ns2 mismatch.

eng-rt: can we get concrete customer impact numbers?

maria (oncall): monitoring shows 502/504 surge for our generation endpoints. Raw numbers: ~9k failed requests/min at peak, p50 latency up 400ms in EU, error rate peaked at 12% for the EU-AP region. Roughly 11 customer orgs with visible errors in last 15m (CS flagged 3 high-traffic tenants).

customer-success: we're already on calls with 2 customers. they're seeing retries and degraded throughput. asking for ETA.

diego_sre: mitigation plan: 1) stop smart-routing fallback cascade by toggling routing-policy:force-local to true for affected services (quick flip) 2) revert the TTL change on the authoritative zone to a safe value (1800) 3) flush edge DNS caches where possible and coordinate with CDN vendor for urgent purge 4) run a canary to verify stable traffic.

maria (oncall): do step 1 now? agree we need to stop the cascade immediately. diego, can you flip the policy?

diego_sre: doing it now. runbook command: ```curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/v1/policies/routing/force-local" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"service":"gen-api", "value":true}'```

diego_sre: response 200. policy toggled. Observability: error rate dropping to 6% in EU within 45s.

meera_infra: I'm rolling the DNS revert to ns-admin now. Command: ```nsupdate -k /etc/bind/Kgeo.+157+000.key <<EOF
server auth-dns-01.internal
zone geo.company.net
update delete gen-eu.geo.company.net. 30 IN A
update add gen-eu.geo.company.net. 1800 IN A 10.2.3.21
send
EOF```

meera_infra: update pushed to ns1 at 10:40UTC. pushing to ns2 now; will confirm once serial increments.

ops-bot: SYSTEM: DNS zone serial increased to 20260315-42 on ns1. Propagation estimate: typical 30-120s given mixed TTLs and vendor caches.

diego_sre: edge cache flush requested with CDN via emergency API: ```POST /v1/purge {"targets": ["gen-eu.*"]}``` vendor responded ack id purge-85f.

eng-rt: we're still seeing a small tail of 502s from older clients (likely cached records). Suggest we also add a temporary routing-policy override: prefer-region=origin for 60s for legacy clients. Thoughts?

maria (oncall): ok do it for 2 mins, can be reverted. Need to balance increased origin load vs continued failures.

diego_sre: override applied. Observability: error rate down to ~1.1% global, EU back to baseline within 3m. p95 latency returning to normal.

customer-success: relayed to customers: mitigation in place, will follow up with RCA. customers relieved, one asked for postmortem and timeline.

meera_infra: ns2 responded at 10:44UTC (serial match 20260315-42). Confirmed no stale rrsets on authoritative pair.

maria (oncall): timeline for postmortem: we'll assemble a preliminary timeline in 2 hours. Action items now: (A) meera to audit the zone update pipeline and why ns2 missed the initial push (B) diego to review routing fallback cascading logic and add a safety throttle (C) eng-rt to create a short eval to simulate mixed-ttl scenarios and measure cascade risk (D) cs to notify impacted customers with ETA for RCA.

meera_infra: noted. initial suspicion: intermittent API timeout to ns2 management endpoint during rollout (we have logs showing a 502 from ns-admin at 10:12:08). will dig in and follow up.

diego_sre: also adding a new guard to the routing controller: if fallback rate > 10% in 60s, cap new fallbacks to 5%/min to avoid cascade. I'll open PR and tag for review.

eng-rt: I'll build a small harness to fuzz TTL mismatches and run it against canary infra this week.

maria (oncall): final status: incident mitigated at 10:47UTC. Full recovery verified by dashboards at 10:50UTC. Recording incident as SEV2. I'll hand off to diego for follow-up. Oncall handover: diego you're primary for RCA items. I'm marking resolved in pager.

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated. Duration: ~35m. Root cause: authoritative zone propagation mismatch (TTL drift) + routing fallback cascade amplification. Next steps: RCA doc + follow-ups assigned.

diego_sre: taking handoff. I'll coordinate the RCA doc and include timeline + code/ops changes. ping me if you have customer notes.

maria (oncall): thanks everyone. :heart: closing channel thread, will add notes to incident tracker.
